elements.text: Think bigger. Build faster.

elements.text: Frequently asked
Can I mix seat types on one plan? Yes. A team can have any combination of Full, Dev, and Collab seats. Collab seats are free on every plan and can comment, view, and edit in FigJam.
Is there a discount for education? Students and educators at accredited institutions get the Professional plan free. Verification takes about two business days.
How does billing work when I add a seat mid-cycle? New seats are prorated to the end of the current billing period and then renew with the rest of the team.
Figma Design
Design, prototype, and iterate in one multiplayer file. No installs, no sync conflicts, no exports to review a change.

children.text: Frames that resize with their content. Set padding, gap, and wrapping once and let the layout do the rest.
Bind colors, numbers, strings, and booleans to variables, then switch light, dark, compact, and comfortable modes with one click.
Build one component with variants and boolean, instance-swap, and text properties instead of a hundred near-duplicates.
Interactive components, smart animate, conditional logic, and expressions turn a static frame into a clickable flow.
Explore an idea on a branch, review the diff, and merge back into the main file when the team agrees.
Every cursor in the file is a teammate. Observe someone, follow along, or hop into an audio conversation.

elements.text: What changed in 2026

Grid auto layout lets a frame lay children on a two-dimensional grid with named tracks. Variables gained typed collections that can be exported as design tokens JSON. Prototype expressions can now read and write variables inside a flow, which makes a working calculator a design file rather than a demo.

elements.text: FigJam
An online whiteboard where the whole team can think out loud. Sticky notes, shapes, connectors, stamps, and a timer that keeps the meeting honest.

children.text: Retrospectives, user journey maps, brainstorms, and sprint planning boards you can start from in seconds.
Flowcharts and system diagrams with connectors that stay attached when shapes move.
Ask for a summary of the sticky notes on a board, sort them into themes, or turn a rough outline into a draft flow.

elements.text: Runs the meeting with you

Start a timer, open a vote, and let everyone drop stamps on the ideas they want to keep. When the session ends, the board is already the record: no one has to type up the whiteboard afterward. Every FigJam board lives next to your design files, so a flow sketched on Monday becomes the frame you design on Tuesday without copying anything between tools.
Dev Mode
A workspace inside every file built for the people who write the code. Measure, inspect, and copy without accidentally moving a layer.

children.text: Designers mark sections ready and Dev Mode shows what changed since the last time you looked.
CSS, SwiftUI, and Compose snippets generated from auto layout and variables, with your token names.

elements.text: Design systems
Variables and modes, one year on
By Mei-Lin Tsao · 2026-06-11

When variables shipped, the question we heard most was whether a design tool needed a type system. A year later the answer from the teams we talked to is a clear yes, and mostly for a reason we did not predict: modes made the cost of a theme visible.

Before variables, a dark theme was a second copy of every screen. It drifted within a sprint. Now a dark theme is a column in a collection, and the diff between light and dark is a list you can read in one sitting. Teams told us they were finally able to delete the second copy.

What is next: expressions in prototypes can now read and write variables, and Grid auto layout uses variables for track sizes. We are working on collection-level permissions so a platform team can own the primitives while product teams own their aliases.

elements.text: Dev Mode
From design to code with Dev Mode
By Rafael Ortega · 2026-03-19

The gap between a design and the code that ships was never about the pixels. It was about the questions: is this ready, what changed, which component is this, and what do we call that color in the codebase.

Dev Mode answers those in order. Ready-for-dev status marks the sections that are done. Compare changes shows the diff since the last time you opened the section. Code Connect maps a Figma component to the real one in your repository so the snippet is your code, not generated CSS.

We recently spent a week with the front-end team at Meridian Health, who use Code Connect for a React library of about sixty components. Their rule is simple: if a component exists in the library, the Figma snippet must show the library import. Engineers stopped writing bespoke buttons within a month.
If you are starting out, connect a repository on GitHub, map the ten components your team uses most, and leave the rest for later. The value shows up on the first pull request.

elements.text: Popular topics
Share a file
Applies to: Figma Design, FigJam · Updated 2026-07-02
1. Open the file and select Share in the top right.
2. Choose who can access: anyone with the link, only people invited, or your organization. Pick the permission: can view, can edit, or can edit in Dev Mode only.
3. Copy the link or type an email address to send an invitation. Invitees who are not on your team join as viewers and do not use a paid seat.
4. To share a single frame, right-click it and choose Copy link. The link opens the file scrolled to that frame.
Manage team billing
Applies to: Figma Design, FigJam · Updated 2026-07-02
1. Team admins open the team page, then Settings, then Billing.

2. The billing page lists every seat by type (Full, Dev, Collab) and the members using it. Change a member's seat type from the dropdown next to their name; the charge is prorated to the end of the current period.
3. To move from monthly to annual billing, choose Change plan. Annual billing is charged up front and shows a credit for the unused part of the monthly cycle.
4. Invoices are available as PDF under Billing history. Add a purchase order number and a billing email if your finance team needs them on every invoice.
